STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole red-yellow apple sitting on a white plate. Not a composed meal; it is a snack/fruit serving.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White oval/triangular serving plate, roughly 24 cm across the long axis, treated as a ~22 cm plate. Area ≈ 3.14 x (11)^2 ≈ 380 cm^2 (oval shape, so roughly 330-380 cm^2 effective).

STEP 3 - Items: one whole apple (red skin, yellowish flesh assumed).

STEP 4 - Area: The apple covers about 14% of the plate area (roughly 9 cm x 8 cm footprint seen from above, ~55 cm^2 of ~380 cm^2 plate area).

STEP 5 - Volume: Whole apple is a solid fruit, not a loose pile. Footprint ~55 cm^2 x height ~7.5 cm ≈ 400 ml envelope; a real apple's volume is closer to its ellipsoid, so use ~200 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit has a density near 0.8-0.9 g/ml (solid, with skin). 200 ml x 0.85 ≈ 170 g. A medium apple of this size typically weighs 150-180 g; use 165 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw apple ≈ 52 kcal/100 g. 165 g x 52 ≈ 86 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single medium apple at ~165 g and ~85 kcal is plausible for what is visible. The apple is the only food on the plate, and no oil, dressing, or other items are visible.

Total: about 165 g, about 86 kcal.
